newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal school bomb kills one, injures five.
newsitem.headline: Portugal school bomb kills one, injures five.

text.p: An explosion that killed one woman and injured five other adults at a school in central Portugal on Friday was caused by a bomb, a police spokesman said.
"It was an explosive device," said the spokesman at police headquarters in Fundao, a small town in the mountainous central region of Portugal, 200 km (125 miles) northeast of Lisbon.
He said there was still no indication as to who placed the device that exploded at 0815 GMT against an outside wall of the primary school, or what the motive was.

Two phone calls were received at the school shortly before the blast, but it was not clear whether they were connected to the explosion as the caller hung up each time without speaking, the police spokesman added.
The dead woman was identified as Ana Maria Nunes, a 32-year-old mother who worked in the school. Three other school employees were also seriously hurt while two more suffered slight injuries.
There were no children hurt in the blast.
Schools have not yet reopened in Portugal after the long summer break and the primary school was in any case in the process of being switched to other premises in the town for the new term.
Education Minister Marcal Grilo immediately travelled to Fundao to visit the school. Afterwards he said that he was "enormously worried" by what had happened.

Such incidents are rare here. Unlike neighbouring Spain, Portugal has has known little in the way of political violence since the turbulent days that followed the 1974 armed forces revolt which re-established democracy after decades of autocratic, right-wing rule.
